fields.name: vptr
fields.evidence: Constructor inlined in the fighter boma builder (g0042, near 0x7100689f88) stores vptr 0x7104f88118 (only class, 112 bytes); module stored at boma+0xC8.

fields.name: owner_boma
fields.evidence: Constructor stores the boma beside the vptr; pickup_item passes it to the pickup callback; item creation reads the owner battle object id at boma+0x8.

fields.name: have_slot_num
fields.evidence: Setup slot +0x28 (f_7100470460) copies 16 bytes from its first pointer arg into +0x10/+0x18; remove_all (+0x150) and slot +0x2A0 loop over this many have slots. Zeroed by the constructor and slot +0x2B8 (clear).

fields.name: have_slots
fields.evidence: Array of held-item slots, stride 0x20, indexed by the slot argument (ITEM_HAVE slot / hand) of every get_have_item_* method.

fields.name: have_node_table
fields.evidence: Setup stores its 4th arg. Item take/throw paths (slots +0x78/+0x88/+0x158/+0x160/+0x1D8/+0x200) load one of 4 u64 entries (+0x0/+0x8/+0x10/+0x18) chosen by item size/hold kind: the joint hash the item is attached to.

fields.name: attach_items
fields.evidence: Setup stores its 3rd arg: a ring buffer of attached items (+0x8 capacity, +0x10 count, +0x18 head, +0x28 data, record stride 0x20 with the item battle object id at +0x0). get_attach_item_count, is_attach_item, drop_attach, drop_attach_group, scale_attach, set_attach_item_action walk it; all tolerate a null pointer.

fields.name: pickup_context
fields.evidence: Setup stores its 5th arg; pickup_item (+0xA8) and slot +0x50 pass it as the first argument of the pickup callback (+0x38).

fields.name: pickup_callback
fields.evidence: Setup stores its 6th arg; unexported setter slot +0x298 stores a pointer. pickup_item calls its vtable +0x10/... with (pickup_context, boma); slot +0x50 calls vtable +0x10 with (pickup_context, this+0x40, boma, 0) to refresh the pickable item info.

fields.name: pickable_item_kind
fields.evidence: get_pickable_item_kind (+0x130) returns it. Constructor and resets (+0x30 / +0x38) set -1 (ITEM_KIND_NONE). Start of a 0x20-byte pickable-item record (0x40..0x5F) that the callback fills and slot +0x118 copies out whole.

fields.name: pickable_item
fields.evidence: get_pickable_item_object_id (+0x120) dereferences it with a null check. Constructor/reset 0.

fields.name: pickable_item_trait
fields.evidence: get_pickable_item_trait (+0x138) returns it. Reset 0 (ITEM_TRAIT_FLAG_NONE).

fields.name: pickable_item_size
fields.evidence: get_pickable_item_size (+0x128) returns it. Reset 2 (ITEM_SIZE_INVALID).

fields.name: pickable_flags_0x58
fields.evidence: Part of the pickable record; resets write u16 1.

fields.name: pickable_value_0x5c
fields.evidence: Part of the pickable record; resets write 0xFE.

fields.name: have_item_param_0x60
fields.evidence: Unexported setter slot +0x2A8 stores an int; the take-item path (slot +0x68 area, f_7100470be0) passes it with the owner id when creating/attaching the item; slot +0x2B8 zeroes it.

fields.name: is_success_pickup_item
fields.evidence: is_success_pickup_item (+0xB0) returns it; pickup_item (+0xA8) stores the callback's result; resets clear it.

fields.name: have_item_visibility
fields.evidence: set_have_item_visibility (export -> slot +0x1C0, f_7100473200) stores it (and forwards to the held item); unexported getter slot +0x1E8 returns it; the take path (f_7100470be0) tests it to set the new item's visibility. Reset slot +0x30 sets 0x65..0x6C to 1; constructor 1.

fields.name: flag_0x68
fields.evidence: Unexported getter slot +0x230 returns it; reset +0x30 sets 1.

fields.name: change_status_event
fields.evidence: set_change_status_event (export -> slot +0x2B0, f_7100474ee0) stores arg&1. Constructor 1.

fields.name: is_success_auto_pickup_item
fields.evidence: is_success_auto_pickup_item (+0xC0) returns it; success_auto_pickup_item (+0xB8) sets 1; resets clear it.

fields.name: have.item_kind
fields.evidence: get_have_item_kind (+0xD8) loads the u32 at slots[slot]+0x0.

fields.name: have.item
fields.evidence: is_have_item (+0xC8) tests it for non-null. get_have_item_id (+0x108) returns item->battle_object_id (+0x8) without a null check; get_have_item_status_param_int/float/bool (+0xF0/+0xF8/+0x100) query the item's +0x228 param object by hash; get_have_item_hold_kind (+0xE8) indexes the global item param table (stride 0xAC) with the item's +0xC kind index, only when is_have_item.

fields.name: have.item_trait
fields.evidence: get_have_item_trait (+0xE0) loads it.

fields.name: have.item_size
fields.evidence: get_have_item_size (+0xD0) loads it.

fields.name: have.item_id
fields.evidence: get_have_item_id (+0x108): fixed pointer path then a plain u32 load (crashes if the slot is empty).

pointers.to: have-item slot records[have_slot_num], stride 0x20 {kind, pad, Item*, trait, size, 8 more}
table of 4 joint hashes used to hold the item
attached-item ring buffer (capacity +0x8, count +0x10, head +0x18, data +0x28, stride 0x20)

notes: One class, 0x7104f88118, 112 bytes. The module holds only pointers to owner-provided tables plus the pickable-item record (0x40..0x5F) and a few flags; item state itself lives in the Item objects. get_have_item_hold_kind/status_param_* and get_shoot_item_bullet are computed through the Item object, not fields. Bytes 0x66, 0x67, 0x69..0x6B are written only as part of the 0x65..0x6C 'all ones' reset (unnamed flags). Setup slot +0x28 args: (have_slots descriptor, attach ring, node table, pickup_context, pickup_callback); it also registers two event listeners on the boma's event manager.
